subject: Private deployment rolling patch - connectivity fluctuation (MediSphere)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medisphere.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed connectivity spike during your rolling patch - private deployment (us-west-2)

Hi Grace,

We started seeing intermittent API connection failures to our private deployment around 08:48 PDT during what our ops console shows as your "rolling patch" window. Errors were 502/504s and also a handful of persistent reconnects for the management/control plane. Our application experienced about ~7% request errors over a 14 minute window; the worker pool auto-recovered after we applied local retries but it's causing user-visible latency.

I attached the timeline and a quick system snapshot from our side (small tar). Can you confirm if that window aligns with any changes on Redwood's side? We need to know:
- Was this an expected transient during the patch?
- Any action recommended on our side to avoid impact during future rolling patches?

Thanks,
Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
SRE Lead, MediSphere Health
liam.oconnor@medisphere.com

Subject: Re: Observed connectivity spike during your rolling patch - private deployment (us-west-2)

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and for the timeline. I'm escalating this to our platform engineers and product leads (cc'd).

Initial notes: our planned rolling patch for private deployments in us-west-2 did include a control-plane agent upgrade that uses a new handshake backoff. We did not expect customer-visible 5xxs, and I'm sorry you saw user impact.

Immediate next steps (we're on it):
- I'm opening a secure bridge now (I'll share dial-in in a follow-up).
- Aditya and Rafael will collect control plane traces and the management agent logs for the 08:40–09:00 PDT window.
- We'll provide a short timeline and a remediation path (canary rollback or targeted restart) by +90 minutes.

Would you be available for a 30 min bridge at 10:15 PDT for a quick triage? If not, tell me the best time.

I attached the logs we asked you for to the ticket and pulled your timeline into the incident record.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Observed connectivity spike during your rolling patch - private deployment (us-west-2)

Grace / team,

I pulled the control plane traces and correlated them with the timestamps Liam sent. Summary:
- At 08:46:03 PDT we see an uptick in handshake timeouts on the conductor-to-agent channel for several tenants in the us-west-2 rolling patch batch.
- The upgrade introduced a change to our keepalive timing that, in a narrow path, increased outbound SYN retries when the host network faced transient packet loss. Those retries bumped response latencies and pushed a small fraction of connections into 502/504 on the management plane.
- Notably, the inference runtime itself remained healthy — token serving succeeded when control plane operations weren't required.

Attachments: controlplane-trace-20270403.json (extracted traces), controlplane-logs-20270403.tar.gz (agent stdout + system metrics).

Recommended remediation (fast):
1) Canary rollback of the new agent on the remaining roll batch (safe, quick, 15–25 min).
2) If you prefer, targeted restart of affected agents on your VPC; this requires a scheduled coordination window of ~10 min and a short maintenance notice.

Longer-term: revert the keepalive change and deploy a more tolerant backoff in next release. I'll open INF-4821 and link the traces.

Grace — if Liam approves a canary rollback, we'll execute immediately and monitor for stabilization. Rafael, can you confirm if there are any commitments that block a rollback?

- Aditya
Lead Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachment(s): controlplane-trace-20270403.json, controlplane-logs-20270403.tar.gz

Grace, Aditya — thanks for the quick analysis.

We'd prefer the canary rollback on your side rather than restarting agents from our end. Please go ahead with the rollback for the remaining hosts in the batch and confirm once the control plane metrics show stability. We will keep retries enabled for 30 minutes and monitor.

Also, because this caused a brief user impact, what's Redwood's process for credits/incident remediation? Our procurement team will ask for a short incident record for billing.

Available for the bridge at 10:15 — joining in a few minutes.

Thanks,
Liam

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & actions — 2027-04-03 private rolling patch (MediSphere)

Liam — thank you again for being responsive during the bridge on Saturday. This thread is the post-incident follow-up and includes the actions we committed to on the call.

What happened (brief):
- During a scheduled rolling patch in us-west-2, a change to agent keepalive/backoff behavior caused increased SYN retry behavior under transient packet loss, producing a small number of control-plane 502/504s for customers in the affected patch batch (including MediSphere).
- The inference runtime remained available for most requests; the visible errors were limited to control-plane dependent operations.

Impact:
- Duration: ~14 minutes (08:46–09:00 PDT)
- Customer-visible request error rate: approx 7% for the window reported by MediSphere
- Scope: subset of tenants in the roll batch in us-west-2 (no data loss)

Immediate remediation taken: 
- Canary rollback executed for remaining hosts in the roll batch at 10:20 PDT on 2027-04-03. Post-rollback monitoring showed control-plane success rates returned to baseline within 6 minutes.
- We coordinated a short targeted restart on two hosts where rejoin jitter persisted.

Artifacts attached / linked: 
- controlplane-logs-20270403.tar.gz (raw agent logs)
- controlplane-trace-20270403.json (extracted traces)
- postmortem-draft-privnet-20270406.pdf (initial customers-facing postmortem)
- Incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-4821
- Shared drive folder: https://redwood.app/drive/shared/postmortems/MediSphere-20270403

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Aditya: revert keepalive change and prepare a compatibility patch for staging (INF-4821) — ETA 2027-04-12
- Rafael: update rolling patch runbook with additional pre-checks and canary abort criteria — ETA 2027-04-09
- Grace: coordinate incident record for procurement and prepare customer-facing statement about credits (if requested) — ETA 2027-04-07

Credits / remediation: if MediSphere requests a billing credit for the outage window, I'll coordinate with our finance team and follow Redwood's incident credit policy. Please let me know the preferred contact from procurement and we will prioritize that request.

Open questions we shared on the bridge:
- Would MediSphere prefer we notify a specific ops contact 24 hours before future rolling patches? (We can add a pre-patch advisory feed.)
- Are you interested in a short postmortem call next week to walk through the logs and the changes?

Thanks again for partnership here. We'll update the shared drive with the final customer-facing postmortem once the engineering changelist is approved.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
